short: Full-inventory phoneme classification on ECoG (M06) is standard: Brumberg 2011 did 38 phonemes intracortically; the 36% headline is consonants only, on hand-labelled onsets.
position: The paper [@mugler2014direct] changes one component: its decoder (M06) classifies phonemes across the General American inventory as events inside spoken words, aligned to hand-labelled phoneme onsets, on ECoG. Against the field of its time this is standard, not ahead: 8 of 11 earlier intracranial speech-unit studies name small subsets of two to six units, but full-inventory classification already existed in Brumberg et al., 38 attempted phonemes at 16–21% against 2.6% chance from an intracortical implant [@brumberg2011classification] (Appendix). The authors' own "first" is scoped to ECoG and holds against the read ECoG priors, which classified four vowels or four phonemes [@pei2011decoding; @leuthardt2011using] (Appendix). The headline overreaches: the abstract's "up to 36% accuracy when classifying all phonemes" is subject NU2's consonant accuracy (36.1%, Sec. 3.1), vowels and consonants were classified separately, and every analysed phoneme, test trials included, sits on an onset placed by hand from the microphone (Sec. 2.4). What the paper does establish is that onset precision governs phoneme decoding (Sec. 3.1); Wilson et al. [later] used the same within-word, hand-labelled protocol on 39 phonemes [@wilson2020decoding].
